pair_convention.spot_explanation: CHF/JPY at 190.48 means 1 CHF = 190.48 JPY. Rising = CHF strengthening vs JPY; falling = CHF weakening vs JPY (equivalently JPY strengthening). The two dossiers quote this cross on opposite conventions: the CHF dossier treats a falling CHF/JPY as a weaker franc, the JPY dossier treats it as a stronger yen. These are the same statement. Every stance, level and scenario is in pair terms only.

executive_summary: CHF/JPY is at 190.47734 on the gated store's 2026-10-02 close. The pair is quoted in yen per franc, so a rising pair means a stronger franc. It is down 1.27% over one month, 5.01% over three and 5.30% over six, and up only 0.35% over twelve. On a closing basis it sits at the 15th percentile of its 52-week range, below a 50/100/200-day moving-average stack that slopes downward. The main bilateral story is that this is the only G10 cross where the base currency yields less than the yen: SNB 0.00% against BoJ 1.25%, a gap of −125bp, and 145bp on the executable futures roll. Over the strategic window the scheduled calendar is three BoJ decisions against one SNB assessment. Neither dossier carries that asymmetry on its own: the CHF dossier is Bearish CHF at −0.3002 and the JPY dossier is only Neutral JPY tactically at −0.0281. The cross becomes a clear signal only at the strategic horizon, where a Bullish JPY score of +0.2497 meets a Bearish CHF score of −0.2566. The settled verdict is Bearish on both horizons: tactically at conviction 2 (score −0.1133), strategically at conviction 3 (score −0.1962). The short side is paid to wait, which no other G10 yen long offers. The tactical caveat is that two 2026-10-01 prints went against the verdict before it was published. Swiss September CPI came in at 1.0%, and the BoJ Summary of Opinions disappointed investors looking for an October move, leaving the yen the worst G10 performer on the day. The pair rose 1.00% that session. In our own judgement the tactical balance is now closer to Neutral than the −0.1133 suggests. The scored verdict stands as issued, and we express it through a small position, entered on rallies.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: CHF/JPY is the only G10 cross in which the base currency yields less than the yen. The SNB policy rate is 0.00% against the Bank of Japan's 1.25% since the 2026-09-18 hike, a bilateral differential of -125bp against the base, so a long CHF/JPY position pays carry rather than earning it. The gated store's CME calendar-spread roll puts the executable cost at 145bp annualised, a 20bp wedge above the policy gap that bounds cross-currency basis and term effects jointly without separating them. The sovereign leg reinforces rather than offsets: the payload's CHF 10-year at 0.47% against the JGB 10-year at 2.94% is a -247bp bilateral discount, and both legs are monthly 2026-08-01 vintages, so with the JGB having risen roughly 141bp over a year against a near-static Swiss curve the live gap is almost certainly wider than the stored one. Trajectory is the decisive bilateral fact: the BoJ has delivered 50bp in 2026 and has three scheduled decisions inside the strategic window, while the SNB has one. Inside the four-week tactical window the authoritative meeting file shows NO scheduled decision for either leg — the BoJ's 2026-10-30 Outlook Report falls one day beyond it — so the differential cannot reprice on a calendar event and simply accrues against the franc.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the question is the direction of the -125bp gap, and the scheduled calendar is lopsided three to one. The gated meeting file puts BoJ decisions on 2026-10-30 (Outlook Report), 2026-12-18 and 2027-01-22 (Outlook Report) against a single SNB assessment on 2026-12-10. Two of the three BoJ dates carry a projection round, which is the vehicle through which a central bank revises its own forecast path and therefore the market's terminal-rate estimate; the SNB's single date carries a quarterly conditional forecast that the Bank has already built on an unchanged 0% rate through 2028. Bloomberg's September survey of BoJ watchers had 93% expecting a follow-up move by January and roughly a third picking December, Trading Economics models project the Japanese policy rate near 1.75% in 2027, and board commentary places neutral closer to 2.00%. On the Swiss side the conditional forecast of 0.7%/0.8%/0.8% is explicitly constructed on no change and economist consensus sides with the Bank rather than the curve. If both house views hold — the SNB validating its own zero and the BoJ delivering two more 25bp moves — the bilateral gap widens from 125bp toward 175-200bp inside the window, and it does so through scheduled, dated events rather than through drift.

Strategically three BoJ decisions — two of them projection rounds — face a single SNB assessment, which is a structural asymmetry in how much policy news each leg can generate, and that asymmetry is what raises confidence.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This factor splits cleanly down the middle and the two halves point in opposite directions, which is what Neutral is for. On inflation the differential favours the yen's policy response: Swiss core at 0.40% on the SNB's reference measure is the lowest in the G10+SGD set, against Japanese core ex fresh food at 1.7% and core-core ex fresh food and energy at 1.9% — a core gap of roughly 130-150bp entirely in the quote currency's favour. On growth the differential is the widest in the set and runs the other way: Swiss Q2 GDP grew 1.885% quarter-on-quarter and 2.632% year-on-year, the fastest and second-fastest in the block, against Japanese growth of 0.36% quarter-on-quarter and 0.73% year-on-year, the lowest in the block. Switzerland's KOF barometer printed a five-year high of 109.1 against a 105.8 consensus while Japan's October Tankan at +24 for large manufacturers MISSED its +25 consensus and non-manufacturers fell to +35 from 37, Japanese industrial production fell 1.7% month-on-month against a +1.4% forecast and household spending fell 3.6% year-on-year. The tactical complication is the Swiss September CPI released on the valuation date at 1.0% year-on-year, above the 0.8% August base and above the SNB's own 0.7% annual path, which narrows the headline inflation gap to Japan's 1.9% and partially validates the December SNB hike pricing. Inflation says sell the pair, growth and the latest Swiss print say buy it, and inside four weeks neither wins.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the reaction-function arithmetic dominates the growth level, and it runs against the franc. A central bank responds to the gap between its inflation measure and its objective: Swiss core at 0.40% against a 0-2% band leaves the SNB with no obligation to move and its own conditional forecast says so through 2028, while Japanese core at 1.7% sits beneath a producer price index running at 7.6% and a corporate services price index at 3.7%, with government energy subsidies mechanically suppressing an electricity component that fell 2.4% year-on-year. The bilateral asymmetry in unpassed cost is the point: Switzerland's producer and import prices are running at -0.70% year-on-year, so there is nothing in the Swiss pipeline to pass through, while Japan carries roughly 5.7 points of producer-over-consumer margin that a subsidy programme is absorbing on the government's balance sheet with an expiry date. Swiss nominal wage growth of 0.40% against a Japanese Shunto settlement of 5.01% for a fourth consecutive year above 5% is the same asymmetry measured in labour costs. Growth remains the counterweight and it is a real one — Switzerland is growing three times faster — but output growth without wage or price follow-through does not move a reaction function, and SECO itself flags that roughly half of Swiss Q2 growth came from the volatile chemical-pharmaceutical sector with second-half moderation expected.

factors.horizon_split: Tactical Neutral becomes strategic Bearish because the two halves of the factor run on different clocks. Over four weeks the Swiss growth beat is loud, the September CPI surprise at 1.0% is fresh, and Japanese demand data are weak enough to offset the Japanese inflation advantage. Over one to six months the Swiss growth level cannot move the SNB without wages or core following, and at 0.40% apiece neither is following, while Japan's 830bp producer-price pipeline and a 5.01% wage round are mechanisms with dates rather than levels.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: CHF/JPY is the G10's only haven-versus-haven cross and therefore has no clean risk beta in either direction: it is not a risk-on pair and it is not a risk-off pair, it is a relative-haven pair whose sign in a shock depends on which refuge the marginal dollar chooses. The current tape denies both legs their mechanism. VIX at 16.07 sits in the lower third of its distribution, US investment-grade spreads at 83bp are near the post-crisis floor, the S&P 500 is up 14.33% year to date and gold — the franc's shared safe-haven proxy and its only commodity link — fell 6.0% over the month, which drains the crisis premium from the one asset that usually corroborates a franc bid. The single crack is US high yield widening 42bp to 302bp against an unchanged investment grade, which is the low-quality end of credit cracking first, but 42bp is not enough to activate a repatriation channel on either side. The bilateral transmission that would matter is the relative size and speed of the two repatriation pools, and they are genuinely comparable: Japanese holdings of foreign securities run roughly USD 3.5 trillion against Swiss foreign assets of CHF 5,564bn, so neither leg has an obvious edge in a scramble. With both channels dormant and the historical evidence split — the yen reacts faster, the franc holds its gains longer — the honest bilateral stance is Neutral.

tactical.what_is_priced: A benign tape with no premium for either haven: a 16.07 VIX and 83bp investment-grade spreads price the absence of an event, and the pair carries no identifiable risk premium in either leg. We agree over four weeks, which is why the stance is Neutral rather than contrarian in either direction.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the asymmetry in the level of credit and volatility is real — 83bp investment-grade and a 16 VIX can widen far more easily than they can tighten — but it is an asymmetry that lifts BOTH legs of this cross, and the pair only moves on the difference. Three considerations keep it balanced. First, the yen's historical VIX beta is the strongest in G10, amplified by carry unwinds, and a shock would normally lift it faster than the franc. Second, that amplification depends on the yen being the funding currency, and it currently is not: speculative positioning has flipped to a net long and desks have rotated funding into the franc, so the mechanical squeeze that normally makes the yen the faster haven now attaches to the franc instead. Third, the specific tails inside the window point in opposite directions — a French sovereign accident with OAT-Bund already at a one-year high of 111.2bp is franc-positive and routes capital into Switzerland rather than the euro area, while a Hormuz re-escalation is a terms-of-trade shock to an economy that sources 94.2% of its crude from the Middle East and is therefore yen-negative even as it is risk-off. Two large, opposing, genuinely live tails on a cross with no net beta is a Neutral with content rather than an absence of view.

factors.horizon_split: Neutral on both horizons with confidence falling two points. The stance is identical because a haven-versus-haven cross has no risk beta at either horizon; the mechanism differs only in that the tactical case is simply the absence of an event, while the strategic case is the presence of two large opposing tails — a French sovereign accident that is franc-positive and a Hormuz re-escalation that is yen-negative — which is a wider distribution around the same zero.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the one factor arguing the pair higher and it argues on a specific, amplified configuration rather than on sentiment. Speculators are short the base and long the quote at the same time, which is the textbook amplification case: CFTC leveraged funds are net short 16,457 CHF contracts at -12.3% of open interest, the most stretched reading in the cached sample, with the all-speculator series having touched the -30,000 contrarian threshold on 2026-09-11 before easing to -26,800; on the other leg, yen non-commercials swung 212.6K contracts from -92.2K net short to +120.4K net long in two weeks and settled at +72.0K, the 88th percentile. Implied CHF/JPY positioning is therefore about as short as the futures market can express it. The flow explanation is documented rather than inferred: desk commentary reports that carry traders have pivoted their funding leg from the yen into the franc as intervention risk and BoJ hikes sapped the appeal of borrowing in yen, with one Bank of America options head stating directly that the market added short franc exposure to fund FX carry trades. CHF/JPY is the purest possible expression of that rotation, which makes it the most crowded short in the complex on both legs at once. Open interest adds fragility: CHF open interest fell 22.1% in the week to 2026-09-22 while the leveraged net extended, and yen open interest collapsed 30% from 542,802 to 378,701 in the same week — a thinner book on both sides of a consensus trade.

tactical.what_is_priced: The market is positioned for CHF/JPY to keep falling and has built that position on both legs simultaneously, which means the marginal seller is scarcer than the flat-looking net on either leg alone suggests. What is not priced is that the covering flow would have to clear a book whose open interest has already fallen 22-30% in a week.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the speculative signal decays to nothing and the two institutional flows that replace it point in opposite directions, which nets to Neutral. On the base leg the franc's net short is its structural resting state — it has been short in every tranche of the cached sample since 2026-04-07 — so there is no long position to revert toward and any squeeze is followed by a rebuild at whatever differential prevails; the carry justifying it against the yen is only 125bp, which is small, but against the rest of the block it is 250-460bp, so the franc gets sold as a funding leg regardless of this cross. On the quote leg the structural flow is genuinely new and genuinely yen-positive: with the JGB 10-year at 3.06% and the 30-year at 4.15%, long-dated Japanese government bonds now out-yield currency-hedged US Treasuries once 3-4% annual hedge costs are applied, which reverses a two-decade outflow from life insurers running 50-60% hedge ratios against roughly USD 3.5 trillion of foreign securities, and the 2027-03-31 Japanese fiscal year-end falls inside the window with its documented repatriation impulse. Switzerland has no comparable institutional turn — SNB sight deposits rose only CHF 2.84bn in the week to 2026-09-25, read as routine liquidity management, and the franc's 0.19% share of allocated global reserves has been flat for five years. The honest offset is that the Japanese flow evidence is not yet confirming: Japanese investors bought 1,082.9bn yen of foreign bonds in the week to 2026-09-16, which is the opposite of repatriation.

strategic.what_is_priced: Consensus treats the Japanese repatriation story as a slow structural narrative with no tradeable timing and treats the franc's short as permanent. factors.horizon_split: Bullish tactically and Neutral strategically because contrarian positioning has a half-life measured in weeks. Over two to four weeks a simultaneous sample-extreme short in the base and an 88th-percentile long in the quote, on a book whose open interest has fallen 22-30% on both legs, is a genuine asymmetry in the pair's favour. Over one to six months the franc's short rebuilds because it is the franc's structural condition, the yen's long normalises toward zero within four to eight weeks of an extreme, and what remains is a Japanese institutional repatriation trend whose weekly data have not yet confirmed it — so the signal nets out.

tactical.combined_positioning_signal: Short base and long quote simultaneously: CHF leveraged net short at -12.3% of open interest (sample extreme, all-spec having touched the -30.0K contrarian threshold) against JPY non-commercial net long at +72.0K contracts and the 88th percentile, after a +120.4K peak that breached the +80K historical extreme. Implied CHF/JPY speculative positioning is maximally short, and unlike a single-leg extreme this one cannot be explained away as the other currency's story.
tactical.unwind_trigger: Three dated or quantifiable triggers, in order of probability: a BoJ hold on 2026-10-30 with no upward revision to the Outlook Report CPI path, which the curve prices at 62-83% and which would force the +72.0K yen long to start liquidating; a French government collapse on the EUR 54bn budget package taking OAT-Bund through 125bp from 111.2bp, which routes capital into francs rather than euros and squeezes the franc short; or a VIX close above 24 from 16.07, which fires both at once.
tactical.historical_analogue: The nearest analogue is the September 2026 yen episode itself, inverted. A 212.6K-contract flip from -92.2K to +120.4K in two weeks demonstrated how violently a one-sided futures book in this complex can reverse when the policy news arrives; the same mechanics now sit on the opposite side of this cross, with the added fragility that open interest fell 22-30% on both legs in the week to 2026-09-22 and the liquidity that would absorb a reversal has already left.
tactical.contrarian_case: The consensus trade is short CHF/JPY, and it is held by two different communities for two different reasons that happen to coincide: real-money yen longs who bought the BoJ normalisation story, and carry desks who rotated their funding leg into the franc. That overlap is what makes the position crowded rather than merely large. The case against the crowd is that the franc short is being added at the very point the SNB's December assessment becomes a coin flip the market prices at 50%, and that the yen long is being held into a meeting the same market prices at under 40% hawkish — both legs are exposed to the opposite outcome of what they are positioned for, and the cross expresses both exposures at once.

strategic.combined_positioning_signal: The speculative configuration dissolves. The franc returns to its structural resting state as a funding short — it has not been net long in any tranche of the cached sample — and the yen long normalises toward zero, historically within four to eight weeks of an extreme. What is left is one institutional flow on each side: Japanese hedged-yield repatriation, which is pair-bearish, and nothing comparable in Switzerland.
strategic.unwind_trigger: For the strategic Neutral to become directional, one of two things must break: Japanese net purchases of foreign bonds turning persistently negative for eight consecutive weeks, which would confirm repatriation and make the factor pair-bearish; or CHF leveraged funds flipping to net long for the first time in the cached sample, which would mark a regime change in the franc's role and make the factor pair-bullish.
strategic.historical_analogue: The 2024 yen episode, in which a comparable positioning flip preceded a sustained period where the yen stopped trading as a pure funding currency. The relevant twist here is that the funding franchise did not disappear, it migrated: desks replaced the yen with the franc as the preferred borrowing leg, which is precisely the rotation documented in August 2026 commentary and the reason CHF/JPY is now the cross where that franchise is priced.
strategic.contrarian_case: The contrarian strategic risk is that the carry community rebuilds the yen short faster than the repatriation flow arrives. Estimates of yen carry positioning run from USD 261bn of direct cross-border borrowing to roughly USD 1 trillion including derivatives, and that structure has reconstituted itself many times on exactly this configuration of low realised volatility and tight credit. If it does, the franc stops being the marginal funding leg, the rotation reverses, and the pair's positioning overhang unwinds in the base currency's favour rather than the quote's.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Raised 0.02 strategically only (0.16 to 0.18). The bilateral terms-of-trade asymmetry here is unusually clean and unusually large: one economy runs a 9.198%-of-GDP current account surplus with energy at 3.5% of its CPI basket, the other sources 94.2% of its crude from the Middle East and has run four consecutive monthly goods deficits into a Brent price 53-56% higher year-on-year. For most crosses this factor is a slow background; for CHF/JPY it is the single largest structural divergence and the main counterweight to the rate story.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The external differential favours the base currency on both the stock and the flow, and the energy channel gives it a live tactical transmission that most balance-of-payments factors lack. Switzerland runs a current account surplus of 9.198% of GDP against Japan's 5.03%, and the composition difference matters more than the level: the Swiss surplus includes a goods surplus of roughly CHF 30bn a quarter, while the entire Japanese surplus rests on a primary income balance of 4,289.6bn yen in July that is reinvested abroad rather than converted, sitting on top of a goods balance that has been in deficit for four consecutive months and printed -1,105.6bn yen in August, the largest since January. That goods deficit is an FX-generative monthly seller of yen; the Swiss goods surplus is an FX-generative monthly buyer of francs. The driver is bilateral in the exact sense this factor requires: Japanese crude imports rose 58.7% and total mineral fuel imports 38.4% year-on-year with Brent near 98-100 dollars, while Switzerland's energy exposure runs through a CPI weight of roughly 3.5% and producer and import prices at -0.70%. Bilateral goods trade itself is small and tilts to the base: IMF DOTS shows Switzerland exporting 9.3bn dollars to Japan against 7.7bn imported, a net 1.6bn surplus in Switzerland's favour on the Swiss-reported basis. The offsetting tactical observation is gold: down 6.0% over the month, and it is the franc's only genuine commodity link.

tactical.what_is_priced: The forward curve prices the external differential at zero, treating the 125bp policy gap and the 145bp roll as the whole of expected return. Over four weeks we broadly agree the surplus does not move spot, but the monthly energy settlement flow does, and the next Japanese current account print on 2026-10-07 is the dated test.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At the strategic horizon this is the strongest single argument for the base currency and the only large positive contribution in the weighted score. Switzerland's surplus is structurally entrenched across three components — a pharmaceutical and precision-manufacturing goods surplus, a services surplus from financial services and commodity trading, and primary income on CHF 5,564bn of foreign assets — and it widened by CHF 13bn year-on-year in Q2 with the net international investment position reaching CHF 986bn. Japan's position is the mirror image in composition: the largest NIIP in the world at roughly USD 3.3 trillion underwriting an income floor, sitting on a goods account that the 2026 Iran war converted into a persistent deficit. The transfer is not a forecast, it has happened: Brent peaked at 118.35 dollars in March, troughed at 71.57 in July and is back near 98-100, which is 53-56% above a year ago, and for an economy importing roughly 99% of its oil and 94.2% of its crude from the region this is a continuing monthly transfer of real income abroad even on flat prices. The competitive trend reinforces it — both South Korea and Taiwan out-exported Japan in H1 2026 for the first time — while Switzerland's export concentration risk runs to the United States at 21.9% and Europe at 49.6%, which is a real vulnerability but not one that is currently firing. Confidence is held at 68 rather than higher because Switzerland is also a net energy importer, because the Japanese surplus WIDENED year-on-year despite the shock, and because the Swiss monthly trade balance itself halved to CHF 3.786bn in the August release.

factors.horizon_split: Bullish on both horizons with confidence rising from 58 to 68 and the weight tripling from 0.06 to 0.18, because balance-of-payments flows accumulate rather than arrive. Over four weeks a single trade print is noise and the gold decline partly offsets the energy asymmetry. Over one to six months four-plus consecutive Japanese goods deficits at 58.7% crude-import growth compound into a measurable transfer against a Swiss surplus that nearly doubled through the same shock, and the weight the framework assigns reflects exactly that compounding.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: CHF has no direct commodity export exposure at all. Its only commodity link is gold, and that runs through shared safe-haven demand rather than trade; gold is down 6.0% over the month, which is mildly franc-negative. Switzerland is a modest net energy importer, but energy is roughly 3.5% of the Swiss CPI basket against about 7% in the eurozone, and Swiss producer and import prices are running at -0.70% year-on-year, so an oil shock transmits to the franc weakly and mostly through the inflation channel rather than the trade channel. Precious metals are 39.9% of Swiss goods exports by value, but that is refining and transit rather than a terms-of-trade exposure.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: JPY is one of the most commodity-exposed currencies in G10 on the import side. Japan imports roughly 99% of its oil and sources 94.2% of its crude from the Middle East; crude imports rose 58.7% year-on-year and total mineral fuels 38.4% in the August data, producing a fourth consecutive monthly goods deficit. LNG via JKM is the second channel, with Asian spot prices having risen more than 140% after the Ras Laffan strike. The framework's direction rules put oil up as strongly negative for JPY and LNG up as strongly negative for JPY, with no offsetting export exposure.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Apply the direction rules leg by leg. Oil up: JPY gets the double-minus (strongly negative) on a 99%-import, 94.2%-Middle-East-sourced energy structure that is already producing monthly goods deficits; CHF gets at most a single minus, and a weak one, because energy is only 3.5% of its basket, it has no commodity export to lose and its producer prices are negative. Net: the quote currency is hurt materially more than the base, so the pair RISES. Oil down: the asymmetry reverses with equal force — Japan's goods deficit narrows sharply, the terms-of-trade transfer stops, and the suppressed-energy component of Japanese CPI falls further, while Switzerland gains only a marginal basket effect but also loses the inflation impulse supporting SNB hike pricing. Net: the pair FALLS, and it falls on both the trade and the policy channel at once. LNG via JKM up: double-minus JPY, neutral CHF, so the pair rises. Gold up: single-plus CHF through shared haven demand, mildly negative JPY through the import bill, so the pair rises; gold's 6.0% monthly fall is therefore the one commodity move currently working against the base currency.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Brent from roughly 98-100 dollars to roughly 108-110. Japanese crude and mineral-fuel import values rise proportionally against a goods balance already running -1,105.6bn yen a month, widening the deficit and the monthly yen-selling settlement flow; Swiss headline CPI rises by a fraction of the Japanese impulse on a 3.5% basket weight, which is mildly supportive of the franc through SNB hike pricing. Net: CHF/JPY RISES, and this is the single cleanest commodity-driven bullish scenario for the pair.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Brent from roughly 98-100 dollars to roughly 88-90. Japan's largest single structural drag eases: the goods deficit narrows, the terms-of-trade transfer slows and the primary income surplus is no longer offset. Switzerland loses the energy pass-through that lifted headline CPI to 1.0% in September and the market's SNB hike pricing weakens with it. Net: CHF/JPY FALLS, with the policy and trade channels reinforcing rather than offsetting — the asymmetry is larger on the downside than the upside.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Brent crude, with JKM LNG a close second. Both act almost entirely through the quote currency's import bill rather than through the base currency, which is what makes the netting unusually unambiguous for this cross: there is no Swiss commodity export to offset the Japanese import exposure, and the only base-currency commodity link — gold — is a haven proxy rather than a trade exposure.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The guidance divergence between these two central banks is as wide as any in G10 and it runs against the base currency. The Bank of Japan guided on 2026-09-18 that it will continue raising policy rates and gradually adjust accommodation as underlying inflation approaches 2%, framing the move as preemptive against upside risks; the Summary of Opinions published 2026-09-30 is more hawkish still, with a majority favouring further hikes, one member arguing to accelerate the pace and another wanting to reach the goal relatively soon. The Swiss National Bank by contrast provides minimal forward guidance by design, meets four times a year, publishes no rate path and no vote split, and in September reverted from June's language about an INCREASED willingness to intervene back to its standard formulation — a central bank signalling comfort with a weaker currency while the franc depreciated roughly 3% trade-weighted since June. The bilateral consequence inside the tactical window is a guidance vacuum on one leg and an active communication programme on the other: between 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-29 the SNB says nothing at all, while the BoJ's Summary of Opinions is already in the market and board commentary continues. Credibility runs the other way — the SNB has the best inflation record in the developed world and the BoJ is the most opaque communicator in G10 — but credibility only moves a cross when it is tested, and the SNB's is being tested by a curve that prices roughly 50% odds of it contradicting its own published forecast within 70 days.

Both gaps are larger than we think they should be, and the Swiss one is larger than the Japanese one, so the resolution skew is pair-negative.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: The weight on this factor nearly doubles strategically and the bilateral asymmetry becomes structural rather than circumstantial. The BoJ holds three decisions inside the window, two of them Outlook Reports on 2026-10-30 and 2027-01-22, and an Outlook Report is a scheduled vehicle for revising the forecast CPI path and therefore the market's terminal-rate estimate; the SNB holds one assessment on 2026-12-10 whose conditional forecast is already constructed on an unchanged 0% rate through 2028. That is a three-to-one asymmetry in opportunities to move a currency through words. The credibility test is also asymmetric in content. The BoJ's test is whether it will keep hiking against political pressure from an expansionary Takaichi administration, and it has already answered twice in 2026 by hiking anyway; a former executive director puts a back-to-back October move at 20-30% and Bloomberg's survey had 93% expecting a follow-up by January, so the distribution around BoJ guidance is skewed hawkish rather than symmetric. The SNB's test is whether it will validate a curve it has implicitly contradicted, and if it does not — our base case, shared by economist consensus — roughly 75bp of priced Swiss tightening comes out of the front end on a single afternoon. Both resolutions push the pair the same way. The honest counterweight, and the reason confidence stops at 64, is that Lombard Odier now expects a December SNB hike and UBS has flagged that the SNB has a record of surprising markets, so the base leg's binary is genuinely two-sided.

We price the opposite on both counts, which is a double divergence pointing the same way for the cross — and it is also the largest single source of error in this verdict, because one 2026-12-10 afternoon can invert the base leg.

factors.horizon_split: Bearish on both horizons with confidence rising from 60 to 64, which tracks the weight rising from 0.07 to 0.12. Tactically the mechanism is a guidance vacuum on the base leg: with no SNB communication for the whole window, Swiss hike pricing can only decay through data, and that decay is pair-negative. Strategically the mechanism is cadence: three BoJ decisions with two projection rounds against one SNB assessment converts a single binary into a sequence, which raises the probability that at least one event delivers the divergence we expect.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The dated event risks inside the four-week window are asymmetric in the base currency's favour, which is the specific reason this small-weight factor carries a stance. The cleanest is France: the OAT-Bund spread at 111.2bp sits at the top of its one-year 59.0-111.2bp range against a 74.2bp average, French debt is 119% of GDP and a EUR 54bn budget package is pending, and the franc rather than the euro is the regional refuge for eurozone sovereign stress — a channel with no Japanese analogue whatsoever. The second is Iran, where the war sits past day 215, Iran's seven-day roadmap has been rejected and the residual dispute is over sequencing; a failure here is a double hit to the quote currency because it is simultaneously a risk event and a terms-of-trade shock to an economy sourcing 94.2% of its crude from the region, whereas for the base currency it is purely a haven bid. Running the other way is the single largest quote-currency event asymmetry in G10: the late-July 2026 coordinated US-Japan intervention, in which Japan sold roughly 8.45 trillion yen with US Treasury participation, converted the yen's floor from a unilateral threat into a two-government commitment, and both Finance Minister Katayama and Treasury Secretary Bessent have signalled readiness to repeat it. That truncates the quote currency's weak tail and therefore caps how far the pair can rise on a yen-negative shock. Swiss domestic political risk is effectively nil — no federal election inside the horizon and Bilaterals III not in force until end-2028.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the two large geopolitical tails become genuinely two-sided and the modal path flips the sign, which is why the stance flattens. The modal Iran outcome is settlement, not escalation: regional crude exports have recovered to 16.328mn b/d, just under 80% of the pre-war baseline and the highest since the war began, Saudi Arabia has restored half its East-West pipeline capacity and the dispute has narrowed to sequencing. A settlement is doubly bearish for this pair — it removes the quote currency's largest structural drag by narrowing the Japanese goods deficit, and it removes the base currency's energy-driven inflation impulse and with it the SNB hike pricing that is currently supporting the Swiss front end. That is a rare case where good geopolitical news is directionally negative for the cross through two independent channels. Against it, the French file remains live inside the window and a government collapse would be the cleanest franc-positive event available, while the Japanese political calendar — an expansionary administration, a December FY2027 budget and a residual snap-election risk — is quote-negative. The two sides are of comparable size and comparable probability, and the coordinated intervention put sits underneath the whole distribution as a cap on pair upside that does not have a mirror on the downside. Expectation-weighted, that is Neutral with real content rather than an absence of view.

What is not priced is the double-counting problem on the base currency: an Iran settlement would be read as simply risk-positive, when for the franc it is also a disinflationary shock that destroys SNB hike pricing — so the pair should fall further on good geopolitical news than a simple haven-beta would predict.

factors.horizon_split: Bullish tactically and Neutral strategically because the tactical value is in two unresolved negotiations with no scheduled resolution, while the strategic value is in a probability distribution whose centre has moved. Over four weeks the French budget vote is live and the Iran talks can fail in a session, both pair-positive. Over one to six months settlement is the modal Iran outcome and it hits the base currency twice — removing the haven bid and the energy-driven inflation impulse supporting SNB pricing — which flattens the expectation-weighted stance to Neutral even though the tails have not changed shape.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The fiscal differential between these two sovereigns is the widest of any G10 pair and it is also, inside four weeks, completely inert — which is a conclusion worth stating with high confidence rather than converting into a manufactured stance. Switzerland is rated AAA by S&P, Fitch, DBRS and Scope and Aaa by Moody's, all Stable, runs a federal budget balance of 0.00% of GDP under a constitutional debt brake, and carries general government gross debt of 38.5% of GDP on a declining path toward 33.5% by 2031. Japan is rated A1 by Moody's, A+ by S&P and A by Fitch, all Stable, and carries debt of roughly 260% of GDP, the heaviest in the developed world. The market charges for that differential in the curve — the Swiss 10-year at 0.47-0.58% against a JGB 30-year at 4.15% — but it has charged for it continuously for years, and a differential only moves a cross when it is repriced. Nothing is repricing it inside the window: no rating review is scheduled on either side, Japanese auctions are clearing with the late-September 40-year sale drawing the strongest demand since 2020 and the 2026-09-30 two-year clearing at 1.964%, and JGB yields actually fell 2.5-4bp across the curve on 2026-09-30 on a fiscal-reassurance report. A quality gap with no catalyst contributes exactly zero.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Strategically the differential acquires a date, and the date is on the quote side. Japan's FY2027 budget is compiled in December 2026 under an administration that has promised an expansionary programme including a food tax cut, and Fitch has publicly stated it will scrutinise that budget for the balance between growth and fiscal discipline. The mechanism that makes this currency-relevant rather than merely fiscal is the composition of the JGB selloff: a 30-year at 4.15% against a 2-year at 1.93% is a 222bp spread that increasingly reflects term premium rather than policy expectation, and rising long yields driven by term premium are currency-NEGATIVE where rising yields driven by normalisation are currency-positive. With roughly half the JGB stock held by the BoJ and each 100bp on the average yield eventually costing roughly 2% of GDP in debt service, the fiscal-monetary circularity is closing at precisely the moment the government wants to spend. Switzerland has no equivalent exposure at any horizon: the debt brake makes the consolidation path a rule rather than a forecast, ten-year funding costs well under 1%, and no spending initiative is pending inside the window. The reason confidence stops at 56 is that this configuration has been true in some form for thirty years without becoming market-relevant, Japanese ratings are Stable at all three agencies, and roughly 90% domestic ownership remains the shock absorber it has always been.

expression_assessment.directional_expression: The verdict is directional and modest in conviction, so the expression should be modest in convexity. Three considerations: the short-pair direction earns 125bp of policy carry and 145bp on the roll, which pays while waiting and argues against a pure premium outlay; both legs are gap-prone, which argues against short-volatility structures in any form; and the back-end surface is flat through a dense event calendar, which argues that longer-dated optionality is relatively better value than short-dated. The missing risk reversal means the skew cannot be priced, so any structure sized on the ATM surface alone is taking unquantified skew risk — a reason to keep the expression simple. The December cluster is the dangerous one: the SNB assessment and a BoJ decision fall eight days apart, with the Japanese FY2027 budget compilation and year-end funding pressure in the same fortnight, so correlated risk on both legs peaks simultaneously rather than offsetting.
expression_assessment.liquidity_note: CHF/JPY is a secondary cross, not a major. There is no listed option on it anywhere, which is why the gated vol is triangulated rather than quoted, and spot liquidity is materially thinner than on either USD leg — particularly in the Tokyo session, where the yen leg trades actively but the franc leg does not. That combination raises gap risk and execution cost relative to expressing the same view through two USD legs, and it is the single clearest practical argument against treating this cross as a substitute for a major in size.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: On a cross with no dollar leg, most of this factor's usual transmission cancels: both the franc and the yen are low-yielding funding candidates and both are exposed in the same direction to the price and availability of dollars. What does not cancel is which of the two the market chooses to borrow, and that choice has demonstrably moved against the base currency. Dollar funding is abundant but expensive — the Fed at 3.75-4.00% after a 12-0 hike, SOFR printing at IORB of 3.90%, central bank liquidity swaps at USD 72mn, quantitative tightening over since 2025-12-01 and the broad dollar index up 1.59% on the month to 120.33 — which is precisely the configuration in which carry trades are funded rather than squeezed. In that environment the marginal funding currency is the lowest-yielding one, and at 0.00% against the BoJ's 1.25% that is now unambiguously the franc. The rotation is documented rather than inferred: desk commentary from August 2026 reports carry traders pivoting to the franc as intervention risk and higher Japanese rates sapped the appeal of borrowing in yen, with hedge funds pushing their net franc short toward a two-month high while reducing yen shorts in the same week. CHF/JPY is where that rotation lands. The 20bp wedge between the 145bp futures roll and the 125bp policy gap bounds basis and term effects jointly and is too small to carry a signal of its own.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the funding channel contains the single largest flow asymmetry between these two currencies, and it sits entirely on the quote leg. With the JGB 10-year at 3.06% and the 30-year at 4.15%, long-dated Japanese government bonds now out-yield currency-hedged US Treasuries once 3-4% annual hedge costs are applied, which reverses the two-decade outflow from Japanese life insurers and pension funds running 50-60% hedge ratios against roughly USD 3.5 trillion of foreign securities; foreign official holdings of US Treasuries fell to a thirty-year low of 13% by July 2026 as the same arithmetic propagated. The mechanism is a dollar-funding-cost mechanism rather than a risk mechanism, so it operates without needing a shock. Switzerland has no counterpart: the Swiss 10-year at 0.47-0.58% does not out-yield anything, Swiss institutions have no hedged-yield reason to repatriate, and the franc's 0.19% share of allocated global reserves has been flat for five years. Two offsets are real. First, hedge costs are set by the short-rate differential and the Fed may have one hike left, so the crossover could be tested before it is confirmed — and the weekly flow data do not yet confirm it, with Japanese investors buying 1,082.9bn yen of foreign bonds in the week to 2026-09-16. Second, year-end balance-sheet constraints widen cross-currency basis and squeeze funding currencies higher, and inside this window that squeeze would lift the franc — the pair-positive seasonal, landing in the same fortnight as the SNB assessment.

tactical.rationale: At tactical weights the pair is decided by four blocks carrying 0.63 of the weight: Policy & Rates at 0.26, Inflation & Growth at 0.18, Flows & Positioning at 0.12 and Risk Appetite at 0.10. Only one of those four resolves with a sign against the base currency, but it is the heaviest, and it does so for a reason specific to this cross rather than borrowed from either dossier: CHF/JPY is the only G10 pair in which the base currency yields less than the yen. The SNB at 0.00% against the BoJ at 1.25% is a -125bp bilateral differential, 145bp on the executable roll, and inside the four-week window the authoritative meeting file shows no scheduled decision for either leg, so the differential cannot reprice on a calendar event and simply accrues. That is the whole of the tactical bearish case, and it is reinforced by the guidance divergence — one central bank explicitly guiding further hikes with a hawkish Summary of Opinions, the other providing no guidance at all and having just dropped its elevated-intervention language — and by the funding channel, where documented dealer evidence shows carry desks rotating their borrowing leg from yen into francs because the franc is now the cheaper funding currency. The two dossier views interact in a reinforcing rather than conflicting way at the top of the book: the base dossier is Bearish CHF at -0.3002 and ranks the franc 11th of 11, the quote dossier is Neutral JPY at -0.0281 and ranks the yen 5th, so a short-base long-quote cross inherits the gap even though neither standalone view is dramatic. What stops the score going further is genuinely bilateral and genuinely strong. Speculators are short the base and long the quote at the same time — CHF leveraged funds at a sample-extreme -12.3% of open interest, JPY non-commercials at the 88th percentile — on books whose open interest fell 22% and 30% respectively in the week to 2026-09-22; that is the amplifying configuration in reverse, and it makes the consensus short the crowded side. Switzerland's 9.198%-of-GDP current account surplus against a Japanese goods balance in deficit for four straight months on 58.7% crude-import growth is a structural offset even at a 0.06 tactical weight. What is priced against what we expect is the edge: the curve has the differential NARROWING, with roughly 50% odds of an SNB hike on 2026-12-10 and at least 0.75% by September 2027 against a BoJ October move at only 17-38%, while both dossiers' house views have the SNB validating its own zero and the BoJ moving faster than priced. The path of least resistance is therefore a slow drift lower in the pair while the carry accrues, with no scheduled catalyst to force it — the first is the BoJ Outlook Report on 2026-10-30, one day beyond the window, which is itself an argument for conviction 2. Dated catalysts inside the window are the CFTC release on 2026-10-02, Japanese labour cash earnings on 2026-10-06, the simultaneous Japanese current account and SNB reserves prints on 2026-10-07, the FOMC on 2026-10-28 and the BoJ one day later. Conviction is 2 because the score clears its threshold by 1.3 points on a book where the largest single contribution is more than half offset, and because the one event that would resolve it falls outside the window. Where we disagree with the tactical verdict (publishable, not re-scored): pass 1 described the 2026-09-30 Summary of Opinions as 'more hawkish still'. The market read it the other way: it disappointed investors who were looking for signs of another move this month, and CHF/JPY rose 1.00% on 2026-10-01 alongside the 1.0% Swiss CPI print. MUFG has since said that December is now seen as the most likely timing for the next BoJ hike, which pushes the quote leg's catalyst further outside the tactical window. On our own reading the tactical balance is closer to Neutral than −0.1133. The verdict stands, and we express that view through size and entry rather than through the score.

strategic.score_interpretation: A net of -0.1962 is a moderate Bearish reading that sits just below the top of the conviction-2 band and at the bottom of the conviction-3 band. Its composition is more informative than its level: -0.3578 of negative contributions spread across four separate factors — Policy & Rates, Guidance, USD Liquidity and Inflation & Growth — against +0.1616 of positives concentrated almost entirely in External Balance. A negative built from four agreeing factors is more reliable than one built from a single dominant line, which is why strategic conviction is 3 against the tactical 2 even though the absolute score difference is only 0.083. The number would need External Balance to move from Bullish 68 to Bullish 100 at its applied weight, or Policy & Rates to fall from 70 to 33 confidence, to return the pair to Neutral; neither is a small adjustment, which is the sense in which this reading is more robust than the tactical one.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the book changes shape without changing direction. Policy & Rates holds 0.26, External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.18 and Guidance from 0.07 to 0.12, while Inflation & Growth falls to 0.10 and Flows to 0.06 — the structural factors take over from the data-flow factors, and three of the four heaviest resolve against the base currency. The dominant mechanism is the scheduled calendar, and it is as asymmetric as any pair in the set: the gated meeting file puts three BoJ decisions inside the window, two of them Outlook Reports on 2026-10-30 and 2027-01-22, against a single SNB assessment on 2026-12-10. An Outlook Report is the vehicle through which a central bank revises its own forecast and therefore the market's terminal-rate estimate; the SNB's one date carries a conditional forecast already built on an unchanged 0% rate through 2028. If the BoJ delivers two of the three — which 93% of surveyed watchers expected by January, with Trading Economics modelling 1.75% in 2027 and board views placing neutral near 2.00% — and the SNB validates its own zero, the bilateral differential widens from -125bp toward -175bp or beyond through dated events rather than through drift. The two dossier views reinforce powerfully here: the base is Bearish CHF at -0.2566 and ranked 9th of 11, the quote is Bullish JPY at +0.2497 and ranked 3rd, a 0.5063 gap that is among the widest available between any two currencies in the set. Three bilateral factors modify those standalone views and they do not all point the same way. The inflation and producer-price differential is a mechanism with a date rather than a level — Japan carries 5.7 points of unpassed producer-over-consumer margin absorbed by an energy subsidy with a roll-off, Switzerland carries producer prices at -0.70% and nothing in the pipeline — which is pair-negative. The funding channel is pair-negative through a Japanese hedged-yield crossover that has no Swiss counterpart and does not require a shock to operate. Against both stands the largest single positive in the book: Switzerland's 9.198%-of-GDP current account surplus with a goods component that nearly doubled to CHF 23.7bn in Q2, set against a Japanese goods balance in deficit for four consecutive months on 58.7% crude-import growth with 94.2% Middle East sourcing. That surplus caps the decline rather than reversing it, which is a conviction-3 statement and not a conviction-4 one. What is priced versus what we expect is the same wedge seen through a longer lens: the curve has the differential narrowing, pricing SNB liftoff before early 2027 at above 90% and at least 0.75% by September 2027 against a BoJ October hike under 40%; our expectation inverts both. The path of least resistance is a stepped decline keyed to the three BoJ decisions, with the December fortnight — SNB on the 10th, BoJ on the 18th, the Japanese FY2027 budget and year-end funding pressure — as the point of maximum two-sided risk. Conviction is 3 because four independent factors agree and the two central banks' calendars make the thesis falsifiable on dated events; it is not 4 because a 9.2%-of-GDP external surplus on the base leg, a AAA-versus-A sovereign gap that is pair-positive, and a single SNB afternoon that can invert the largest input all argue for restraint.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Among short-CHF expressions, short CHF/JPY ranks 3rd strategically. The CHF-to-JPY score gap of 0.5063 (-0.2566 against +0.2497) trails only CHF/NOK at 0.5307 and CHF/SEK at 0.5142, and sits ahead of CHF/SGD, CHF/AUD and the dollar and euro crosses. Among long-JPY expressions it ranks 3rd on raw score gap — behind short CAD/JPY at 0.6143 and short EUR/JPY at 0.5197 — but 1st on risk-adjusted economics, because it is the only yen long in G10 that is paid to wait: short CHF/JPY earns 125bp of policy carry and 145bp on the roll, where short CAD/JPY pays 100bp, short EUR/JPY pays 125bp and short USD/JPY pays 275bp. Both dossiers independently nominate this cross as their preferred relative-value expression — the CHF dossier names CHF/JPY as the cleanest long-franc hedge if its own view is wrong, the JPY dossier names it as the cleanest long-yen expression outright — which is an unusual degree of agreement from two documents written against each other.

consensus_divergence.our_tactical_view: Bearish, net weighted score -0.1133, conviction 2, overall confidence 57. Direction and conviction only; pass 1 sets no level. Pass-2 level: 188.20 at one month.
consensus_divergence.our_strategic_view: Bearish, net weighted score -0.1962, conviction 3, overall confidence 62. Direction and conviction only in pass 1. Pass-2 levels: 185.50 at three months and 182.00 at six months.
consensus_divergence.divergence_direction: In line on direction at both horizons. The only sourceable consensus path for this cross (Exchange Rates UK, direction only; not a bank forecast) is lower, and so are we.
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: Not quantifiable. The only consensus path located (Exchange Rates UK: roughly 182.90 at one month, 179.86 at three, 175.67 at six, 167-168 by Q1 2027) is anchored on a spot of 202.84 against the gated store's 190.47734, about 1,240 pips higher, so no pip or percentage divergence can be stated honestly; the magnitude disagreement is recorded as unmeasurable rather than estimated. Against the forwards (190.70 / 191.17 / 191.85) our levels are bearish by 250, 567 and 985 pips.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: The substantive disagreement is not about direction but about which leg does the work and over what sequence. The sourceable consensus path front-loads the move, implying most of the decline is already underway. Our tactical conviction is only 2 because the one factor arguing the other way — a simultaneous sample-extreme short in the base currency and an 88th-percentile long in the quote, on books whose open interest fell 22% and 30% in a single week — is a real near-term liability that a level-based consensus does not model, and because the first event capable of resolving it, the BoJ Outlook Report on 2026-10-30, falls one day beyond the tactical window. We also weigh two things more heavily than a standard rate-differential model would. First, the bilateral terms-of-trade asymmetry: 94.2% Middle East crude dependence on one leg against a 3.5% CPI energy weight and a 9.198%-of-GDP surplus on the other is the main reason our strategic score stops at -0.1962 rather than running further, where consensus appears to treat the Swiss surplus as inert. Second, we weigh the SNB's own conditional forecast against the curve: the market prices roughly 75bp of Swiss tightening the SNB says is unnecessary, and an uneventful 2026-12-10 assessment removes it — a base-leg repricing that no CHF/JPY forecast we located articulates. Institutional support is strongest on mechanism rather than level: Russell Investments and Allianz Global Investors favour the franc as a funding source on widening Swiss–Japanese policy divergence. MUFG's October view is that a sustained turn toward yen appreciation requires continued BoJ hikes and restored confidence in fiscal discipline; we weigh that fiscal condition less heavily than MUFG does and price it as a 15% pair-positive risk in Factor 8. No major-bank CHF/JPY target was located; LongForecast, WalletInvestor and 30rates are algorithmic extrapolation scripts and are excluded.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: The thesis is paid in three ways that do not require a large move. The policy carry of 125bp and the 145bp roll accrue to the short-pair direction while waiting, which is unique among G10 yen longs. The differential itself widens toward 175-200bp if the BoJ delivers two of three and the SNB holds. And the Swiss front end reprices lower on an uneventful December assessment, which moves the base leg without needing anything from Japan.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: Two distinct failure modes, and they are not symmetric. The tactical failure is a positioning squeeze: a crowded short on both legs, into an open-interest base already down 22-30%, unwinds violently on a BoJ hold with no Outlook Report upgrade, on a French budget resolution, or on any VIX spike that squeezes franc shorts. The strategic failure is the SNB hiking on 2026-12-10 — Lombard Odier now expects exactly that and the curve prices it at roughly 50% — which inverts the largest single input in the base leg and would be compounded if an Iran settlement simultaneously narrowed Japan's goods deficit. The second mode is the dangerous one because both legs would move the same way at once.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: Both horizons are Bearish and the strength increases with the horizon, which is the opposite of the usual decay and is explained by the calendar rather than by enthusiasm. The tactical score (net −0.1133, conviction 2, confidence 57) barely clears its threshold and is built on a single dominant negative — Policy & Rates at -0.1716 — more than half offset by positioning and the external account, so four of ten factors resolve Neutral and a six-point confidence change anywhere would return it to Neutral. The strategic score (net −0.1962, conviction 3, confidence 62) is built on four agreeing negatives against one large positive, which is a more reliable construction at a similar distance from zero. Four factors change stance across the horizons: Inflation & Growth from Neutral to Bearish as the producer-price pipeline and wage asymmetry outlast the Swiss growth beat, Flows & Positioning from Bullish to Neutral as the contrarian signal decays and the Japanese repatriation flow replaces it, Event Risk from Bullish to Neutral as the modal Iran outcome turns pair-negative, and Fiscal & Sovereign from Neutral to Bullish as the Japanese FY2027 budget acquires a date.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: The two horizons are compatible and should be sequenced rather than traded against each other. The tactical reading says the direction is right but the timing is poor: no scheduled decision for either currency falls inside the four-week window, the first repricing event is the BoJ Outlook Report on 2026-10-30 one day beyond it, and speculative positioning is crowded on the same side as the thesis on both legs simultaneously. That argues for smaller size early and for treating any positioning-driven move against the view as an improvement in entry rather than evidence of error. The strategic reading says the mechanism is dated and falsifiable — three BoJ decisions against one SNB assessment — and that the short-pair direction is paid 125bp of carry to wait, which is a rare luxury in a yen long. The December fortnight, with the SNB on the 10th, the BoJ on the 18th, the Japanese FY2027 budget and year-end funding pressure all inside eight days, is where correlated risk on both legs peaks and where the position is most exposed. Implementation: tactical half a risk unit sold into 191.50–192.30 with a stop on a daily close above 193.40; strategic one unit built in thirds with a stop on a weekly close above 196.80; if the tactical stop triggers on positioning alone (no SNB news) treat it as a strategic re-entry opportunity toward 194.00, not a thesis failure; reduce strategic size by one third ahead of the 2026-12-10 SNB assessment and rebuild after it.

assumptions: Price series as delivered: 130 daily bars (2026-04-06 to 2026-10-02), spot 190.47734, spotDate 2026-10-02; computation range 2007-12-24 to 2026-10-02 (4900 weekday bars; 1007 weekly, 500 monthly). The 130 daily bars cover the 1-6 month strategic horizon.

Spot date (2026-10-02) is one session after the 2026-10-01 valuation date. Every level, pip calculation, percentage and moving-average distance is anchored to 190.47734. No web spot quote was substituted. The dossiers' CHF/JPY reference of 188.64849 (2026-09-29) is not used for levels.

Moving averages are simple averages of trading-day closes over the whole stored history; realised volatility is annualised on 252 days. The dossiers' 60-day realised of 8.28% ends 2026-09-29; the store's 8.48% is the source of truth in the pass-2 sections; the verbatim pass-1 text retains 8.28%.
Zone distances are to zone midpoints and zones are ranked by touch count. Web-sourced support/resistance levels were not used, except to note that a mid-August commentary level near 192.6 failed.

Factors and synthesis are carried verbatim from pass 1 including weight adjustments (F1 +0.02 both horizons, F4 +0.02 tactical, F5 +0.02 strategic, F10 −0.04 both horizons; both columns sum to 1.00) and every stance, confidence, evidence type and contribution. Pass-1 citation IDs [1]–[13] are retained; sources [14] onward were accessed in pass 2.
Scenarios, targets, stops, sizing, path, ladders, risk/reward, forwards, invalidators and signposts are pass-2 work based on the price payload. None of it feeds back into any stance.

Arithmetic flag: the verbatim Factor 1 carry block states six-month accruals of 0.52% (policy) and 0.60% (roll); straight-line arithmetic on 125bp and 145bp gives 0.625% and 0.725%. Pass-2 sections use the corrected figures; the stance is unaffected.
Forward outrights are derived linearly from the 145bp roll (30/91/182 days) and are not quotes. The roll bundles policy differential, basis and term effects.

Implied volatility figures (8.027% / 7.724% / 7.759%) are triangle estimates (implied correlation 0.5396), documented to run 8.7–17.8% low, and are treated as a floor. No CHF/JPY risk reversal or cross-currency basis exists from a free source. The USD/JPY yen-call skew read-across is directional context only.

Scenario construction: tactical levels are sized to 20-day realised volatility (roughly 490 pips of one-sigma over 20 sessions); strategic levels are tied to structure (base case stops at the rising 200-week, about 181.8 by end-March 2027); the extension case uses the cross-implied level of the dossiers' strategic USD/JPY and USD/CHF targets (151.00 / 0.8520 ≈ 177.2).

Disagreement disclosure: the tactical disagreement rests on two 2026-10-01 events, the Swiss 1.0% CPI print and the market's dovish read of the BoJ Summary of Opinions. It is disclosed in prose and did not alter any score.

Excluded sources: algorithmic forecast pages (LongForecast, 30rates, WalletInvestor, CoinCodex, TradersUnion, AUDToday) as a category error for consensus; a Stockpil summary of an ING note, excluded because it describes the BoJ as 'ultra-loose', contradicting the 1.25% policy rate. No bank consensus forecast could be sourced, so bank_consensus_forecast is null; the Exchange Rates UK path is used for direction only.
Bilateral trade is taken directly from the IMF DOTS block: Swiss-reported $9.3bn exports and $7.7bn imports, a net +$1.6bn. The Japanese mirror report differs and is noted, not reconciled.

Formatter mapping notes: base_cftc_percentile is set to 0 because the source describes the CHF leveraged net short as the cached-sample extreme (no explicit percentile was stated); iv_percentile is null because the report gives no IV percentile; annualised_carry_bps uses the −125bp policy carry to agree with the stated carry-to-vol ratio of −0.162 (the executable roll is −145bp for a long pair); range_52w_percentile uses the 19th-percentile intraday figure (15th on closes); dossier dates are set to the 2026-10-01 valuation date as the report does not state them separately.
Strategic stance on Factor 4 contrarian_analysis and all pair_price_action evidence is confined to Factor 9, per the evidence-type rule.
